lessons.title: Introduction to Generics
lessons.content: Generics let you write classes/functions that work with any type while preserving compile-time type safety. Real scenario: a single Repository<T> pattern reused for Users, Lessons, and Quizzes.

codeSnippets.code:
class Box<T>(val content: T)
val intBox = Box(42)

lessons.title: Generic Functions
lessons.content: A function can declare its own type parameter, inferred from arguments at the call site. Real scenario: a generic parseJson<T>(json: String): T helper reused across many data types.

codeSnippets.code:
fun <T> firstOrDefault(list: List<T>, default: T): T =
    if (list.isNotEmpty()) list.first() else default

lessons.title: Generic Classes
lessons.content: A class declares type parameters used throughout its properties and methods. Real scenario: your app's ApiResult<T> sealed class, written once, reused for every response type.

lessons.title: Generic Constraints (Upper Bounds)
lessons.content: Restrict a type parameter to subtypes of a bound using <T : Bound>. Real scenario: findMax<T : Comparable<T>> only accepts comparable types, caught at compile time.

codeSnippets.code:
fun <T : Comparable<T>> findMax(items: List<T>): T =
    items.reduce { a, b -> if (a > b) a else b }

lessons.title: Variance Overview
lessons.content: Variance describes how generic types with different arguments relate - invariant by default unless out/in is declared. Real scenario: Repository<out T> allowing Repository<PremiumUser> where Repository<User> is expected.

codeSnippets.code:
class Box<T>(val value: T) // invariant
class Producer<out T>(val value: T) // covariant

lessons.title: Covariance (out)
lessons.content: out T marks a type as covariant, usable only in return positions. Real scenario: a read-only DataSource<out T> where every method returns T, none consume it.

lessons.title: Contravariance (in)
lessons.content: in T marks a type as contravariant, usable only in parameter positions. Real scenario: Comparator<Animal> usable wherever Comparator<Dog> is expected.

lessons.title: Star Projections
lessons.content: SomeType<*> means 'a SomeType of some unknown type', used when you don't need to know the type argument. Real scenario: a logging function accepting any Repository<*>.

lessons.title: Reified Type Parameters
lessons.content: inline fun <reified T> preserves type info at the call site, enabling type checks otherwise impossible due to JVM erasure. Real scenario: a type-safe Gson.fromJson<T>() wrapper.

codeSnippets.code: inline fun <reified T> List<*>.filterTyped(): List<T> = filterIsInstance<T>()
